# PART 1: CORE GUIDES & WORKFLOWS

# 5-Minute Quickstart Guide

> Add Kromium to your Gradle project, bootstrap the Chromium engine, and create your first browser instance.

- **Category:** Getting Started
- **Read Time:** 5 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-09-27

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Kromium, ensure your environment meets the minimum runtime requirements:
- **JDK:** Java 17 or higher (Java 21 LTS recommended, e.g., Eclipse Temurin).
- **Supported Operating Systems:**
  - **Windows:** 10 / 11 (x86_64, ARM64)
  - **macOS:** 12+ Monterey, Ventura, Sonoma, Sequoia (Intel x86_64, Apple Silicon ARM64)
  - **Linux:** Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, Fedora, Arch (x86_64, ARM64) with GTK 3+ installed.

## Adding Gradle Dependencies

Add Kromium to your build.gradle.kts using either Gradle Version Catalog or direct coordinates.

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    val kromiumVersion = "1.0.0.150-b11"
    
    implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-api:$kromiumVersion")
    implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-provider-jcef:$kromiumVersion")

    // Target UI integration:
    implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-compose:$kromiumVersion")
    // implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-swing:$kromiumVersion")
    // implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-javafx:$kromiumVersion")
    // implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-swt:$kromiumVersion")
    // implementation("org.daviante.kromium:kromium-awt:$kromiumVersion")
}
```

## Basic Engine Lifecycle & First Browser

Kromium separates the engine lifecycle into three clean stages:
1. **KromiumEngine**: Manages the underlying native Chromium runtime, process models, and shared cache.
2. **KromiumClient**: Represents an isolated session (cookies, storage, and global listeners).
3. **KromiumBrowser**: Represents a single web page view and its control facades.

```kotlin
val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .browserConfig { b ->
        b.cachePath(File(System.getProperty("user.home"), ".myapp-cache").absolutePath)
    }
    .build()

// 1. Instantiate and initialize engine
val engine = Kromium.createEngine(config)
engine.initialize() // Suspends until native runtime is extracted and ready

// 2. Create isolated client session
val client = engine.createClient()

// 3. Create browser instance for your UI toolkit
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.SWING
)
```

## Controlling the Browser

Once created, browser exposes dedicated facades for all web operations: navigation, DevTools, downloads, cookies, and automation.

```kotlin
// --- Navigation ---
browser.navigation.loadUrl("https://github.com")

// Suspending load (waits until DOM is ready):
val loaded = browser.navigation.loadUrl(
    url = "https://github.com",
    waitUntil = NavigationStage.LOADED,
    timeoutMs = 15_000L
)

// --- DevTools ---
browser.devTools.openDevTools()
```

## Observing Reactive Navigation State

browser.navigation.navigationState is a coroutine StateFlow<KromiumNavigationState> that continuously emits real-time loading updates.

```kotlin
scope.launch {
    browser.navigation.navigationState.collect { state ->
        println("URL: ${state.url}")
        println("Page Title: ${state.title}")
        println("Is Loading: ${state.isLoading}")
        println("Can Go Back: ${state.canGoBack}")
        println("Can Go Forward: ${state.canGoForward}")
    }
}
```

## Related APIs

- [Kromium](/llms/api/kromium.md)
- [KromiumEngine](/llms/api/kromium-engine.md)
- [KromiumBrowser](/llms/api/kromium-browser.md)
- [KromiumClient](/llms/api/kromium-client.md)

# Multi-Framework UI Integration Guide

> Learn how to embed Kromium's off-screen rendering (OSR) surface in Jetpack Compose, Swing, JavaFX, SWT, and AWT.

- **Category:** UI Integrations
- **Read Time:** 10 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Supported UI Frameworks

Kromium features a decoupled Off-Screen Rendering (OSR) engine that streams raw Chromium BGRA pixel buffers directly into the native graphical surface of your chosen UI toolkit.

| Framework | Target Module | Framework Identifier | Canvas Surface |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compose Multiplatform** | `kromium-compose` | `KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE` | `KromiumView` Composable |
| **Swing** | `kromium-swing` | `KromiumUiFramework.SWING` | `KromiumSwingCanvas` (`JPanel`) |
| **JavaFX** | `kromium-javafx` | `KromiumUiFramework.JAVAFX` | `KromiumJavaFxCanvas` (`StackPane`) |
| **Eclipse SWT** | `kromium-swt` | `KromiumUiFramework.SWT` | `KromiumSwtCanvas` (`Canvas`) |
| **Pure AWT** | `kromium-awt` | `KromiumUiFramework.AWT` | `KromiumAwtCanvas` (`Canvas`) |

## Compose Multiplatform Integration

The kromium-compose module provides the declarative @Composable KromiumView component with built-in reactive navigation state collection.

```kotlin
val client = engine.createClient()
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE
)

// In your Composable hierarchy:
KromiumView(
    browser = browser,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()
)
```

## Java Swing Integration

In Swing applications, Kromium unwraps into a standard javax.swing.JPanel component.

```kotlin
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.SWING
)

val panel = browser.view.surface.unwrap(Component::class) as JPanel
frame.contentPane.add(panel, BorderLayout.CENTER)
```

## JavaFX Integration

For JavaFX applications, Kromium provides hardware-accelerated texture blitting into a JavaFX Region.

```kotlin
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.JAVAFX
)

val fxNode = browser.view.surface.unwrap(javafx.scene.Node::class)
rootStackPane.children.add(fxNode)
```

## Eclipse SWT Integration

For Eclipse SWT/RCP applications, `kromium-swt` provides `KromiumSwtCanvas` which renders Chromium frames into an SWT `Canvas` widget using an internal `SwtOsrBuffer`. A keyboard bridge handles SWT-to-CEF key event translation automatically.

```kotlin
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.SWT
)

val swtCanvas = browser.view.surface.unwrap(org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Canvas::class)
// Add the canvas to your SWT Composite layout
val layoutData = GridData(SWT.FILL, SWT.FILL, true, true)
swtCanvas.layoutData = layoutData
parent.layout(true, true)
```

## Pure AWT Integration

For lightweight Pure AWT applications without Swing dependencies, `kromium-awt` provides `KromiumAwtCanvas` which renders directly into a `java.awt.Canvas` component using Java2D `BufferedImage` blitting.

```kotlin
val browser = client.createBrowser(
    url = "https://example.com",
    framework = KromiumUiFramework.AWT
)

val awtCanvas = browser.view.surface.unwrap(java.awt.Canvas::class)
val frame = Frame("Kromium AWT Browser")
frame.add(awtCanvas, BorderLayout.CENTER)
frame.setSize(1280, 800)
frame.isVisible = true
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumUiFramework](/llms/api/kromium-ui-framework.md)
- [KromiumView](/llms/api/kromium-view.md)
- [KromiumRenderSurface](/llms/api/kromium-render-surface.md)

# Cloudflare R2 Maven Repository Guide

> How Kromium packages are published to Cloudflare R2 and how downstream projects configure their Maven / Gradle builds.

- **Category:** Deployment
- **Read Time:** 6 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-09-27

## Overview & Architecture

Kromium publishes standard Maven repository layouts directly to Cloudflare R2 under https://repo.daviante.org/artifacts.

### Benefits of Cloudflare R2
- **Zero Egress Fees:** $0 for outbound data transfer.
- **S3-Compatible API:** Operates seamlessly with standard build tools.
- **Edge Caching:** Fast global distribution via Cloudflare's CDN.

## Configuring Downstream Projects

To consume Kromium artifacts in downstream Gradle or Maven projects, add the repository URL to your repository configuration.

```kotlin
// settings.gradle.kts or build.gradle.kts
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven("https://repo.daviante.org/artifacts")
}
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumEngineDownloadConfig](/llms/api/kromium-engine-download-config.md)

# Web Automation & DOM Interaction API

> Playwright-inspired automation engine for SPAs, MutationObserver-backed waiting, form filling, and keystroke dispatch.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 7 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-09-27

## Waiting for Elements & URLs

Kromium's waitForSelector injects an in-V8 MutationObserver to avoid IPC polling overhead, resuming your coroutine the millisecond the element appears.

```kotlin
// Suspends until element matching CSS selector appears
val found = browser.automation.waitForSelector(
    selector = "#login-form",
    timeoutMs = 10_000L
)

// Wait for redirect to dashboard
val redirected = browser.automation.waitForUrl(
    pattern = "https://app.example.com/dashboard",
    timeoutMs = 15_000L
)
```

## Form Inputs & Keystroke Simulation

Automate forms using fill, type, selectOption, and click.

```kotlin
// Instant fill (dispatches input and change events)
browser.automation.fill("input#username", "admin@company.com")

// Human-like keystroke typing with delay
browser.automation.type("input#password", "secret", delayMs = 50L)

// Select option
browser.automation.selectOption("select#country", "US")

// Click button
browser.automation.click("button[type='submit']")
```

## DOM Extraction & State Querying

Inspect DOM properties and content directly without writing raw JavaScript strings.

```kotlin
val text = browser.automation.getTextContent("h1.title")
val href = browser.automation.getAttribute("a#download-link", "href")
val isVisible = browser.automation.isVisible(".modal-dialog")
val totalItems = browser.automation.count(".item-row")
```

## JavaScript Bridge & Async Evaluation

Execute arbitrary JavaScript and await results via browser.jsBridge.

```kotlin
val result = browser.jsBridge.evaluateJavaScript("window.innerWidth * window.devicePixelRatio")
val html = browser.jsBridge.getHtml()
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumAutomation](/llms/api/kromium-automation.md)
- [KromiumJsBridge](/llms/api/kromium-js-bridge.md)

# Enterprise Networking & Proxies API

> Configure HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5, and PAC proxies, remote DNS leak protection, and dynamic proxy switching.

- **Category:** Networking
- **Read Time:** 6 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-09-27

## Supported Proxy Modes

Kromium models proxy configurations via the type-safe sealed class KromiumProxy.

| Mode | Class | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Default** | `KromiumProxy.System` | Adopts host OS proxy settings. |
| **Direct** | `KromiumProxy.Direct` | Bypasses all proxies. |
| **Auto-Detect** | `KromiumProxy.AutoDetect` | Uses WPAD via DHCP and DNS queries. |
| **PAC Script** | `KromiumProxy.Pac(pacUrl)` | Downloads and evaluates PAC script. |
| **HTTP / HTTPS** | `KromiumProxy.Http(...)` | Standard HTTP or TLS-encrypted forward proxy. |
| **SOCKS5 / SOCKS4** | `KromiumProxy.Socks5(...)` | SOCKS proxy with optional remote DNS leak protection. |
| **Multi-Protocol** | `KromiumProxy.MultiProtocol(...)` | Routes different protocols through separate endpoints. |

## Configuring Proxies

Configure the proxy when building KromiumConfig before engine startup.

```kotlin
val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .browserConfig { b ->
        b.proxy(
            KromiumProxy.Http(
                host = "proxy.corp.internal",
                port = 8080,
                username = "corporate_user",
                password = "secure_password",
                isSecure = true,
                bypassList = listOf("<local>", "127.0.0.1", "*.internal.net")
            )
        )
    }
    .build()
```

## SOCKS5 with Remote DNS Leak Protection

Setting remoteDns = true ensures DNS queries are resolved exclusively through the proxy rather than leaking to local ISP.

```kotlin
val socks5 = KromiumProxy.Socks5(
    host = "10.0.0.1",
    port = 1080,
    remoteDns = true
)
```

## Dynamic Runtime Proxy Switching

Switch proxies dynamically on active client sessions without restarting the engine.

```kotlin
val proxyManager = client.proxyManager
proxyManager.setProxy(KromiumProxy.Direct)
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumProxy](/llms/api/kromium-proxy.md)
- [KromiumProxyManager](/llms/api/kromium-proxy-manager.md)

# Downloads, Permissions & SSL Security API

> Intercept downloads, handle camera/microphone permissions, and enforce SSL certificate policies and domain whitelists.

- **Category:** Security
- **Read Time:** 6 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-09-27

## File Download Management

Control file downloads with beforeDownloadListener to customize target paths or cancel downloads, and downloadListener to track real-time progress.

```kotlin
client.beforeDownloadListener = KromiumBeforeDownloadListener { item, suggestedFileName ->
    if (suggestedFileName.endsWith(".exe")) {
        return@KromiumBeforeDownloadListener "" // Cancel download
    }
    File(downloadsDir, suggestedFileName).absolutePath
}

client.downloadListener = KromiumDownloadListener { item ->
    println("Progress: ${item.percentComplete}%")
}
```

## Camera, Microphone & Device Permissions

Intercept WebRTC camera, microphone, and screen share requests via KromiumPermissionListener.

```kotlin
client.permissionListener = KromiumPermissionListener { request ->
    if (request.origin.endsWith("meet.google.com")) {
        KromiumPermissionDecision.GRANT
    } else {
        KromiumPermissionDecision.DENY
    }
}
```

## SSL/TLS Certificate Policies

Configure certificate validation error handling using SslErrorPolicy.

```kotlin
val config = KromiumClientConfig.builder()
    .sslErrorPolicy(SslErrorPolicy.allowDomains("*.corp.internal", "localhost"))
    .build()
```

## Domain Sandboxing & Host Locking

Lock the browser to navigate strictly within an allowed set of hostnames or domains.

```kotlin
browser.security.hostLock = setOf("app.internal.net", "accounts.google.com")
browser.security.hostLockSubresources = true
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumSecurity](/llms/api/kromium-security.md)
- [SslErrorPolicy](/llms/api/ssl-error-policy.md)
- [KromiumPermissionListener](/llms/api/kromium-permission-listener.md)
- [KromiumDownloads](/llms/api/kromium-downloads.md)

# Cookie & Storage Management

> Read, set, and delete cookies, clear browser cache, and manage Local Storage via KromiumCookieManager and KromiumStorage facades.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 6 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Global Cookie Manager

The engine-level `KromiumCookieManager` provides full cookie CRUD operations across all domains. Access it via `engine.cookieManager`.

| Method | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `getCookies(url)` | Retrieves all cookies for a URL as key-value map (suspend) |
| `getCookie(url, name)` | Retrieves a specific cookie by name (suspend) |
| `getAllCookies()` | Retrieves all cookies across all domains (suspend) |
| `setCookie(url, name, value, ...)` | Sets a cookie with domain, path, secure, httpOnly, expiry |
| `deleteCookie(url, name)` | Deletes a specific cookie |
| `clearCookies()` | Deletes all cookies from the store |
| `flush()` | Flushes the cookie store to disk for persistence |

```kotlin
// Read all cookies for a URL
val cookies = engine.cookieManager.getCookies("https://example.com")
println("Session: ${cookies["session_id"]}")

// Set a secure, HTTP-only cookie with expiry
engine.cookieManager.setCookie(
    url = "https://example.com",
    name = "auth_token",
    value = "jwt_value_here",
    domain = ".example.com",
    path = "/",
    isSecure = true,
    isHttpOnly = true,
    expires = Date(System.currentTimeMillis() + 86_400_000L)
)

// Delete and flush
engine.cookieManager.deleteCookie("https://example.com", "auth_token")
engine.cookieManager.flush()
```

## Browser-Level Storage Facade

Each browser instance also exposes a `KromiumStorage` facade (`browser.storage`) for per-page cookie and web storage operations including clearing Local Storage, Session Storage, and browsing data.

```kotlin
// Set a cookie from browser context
browser.storage.setCookie(
    name = "theme",
    value = "dark",
    domain = ".myapp.com"
)

// Clear all web storage (Local Storage + Session Storage)
browser.storage.clearWebStorageAsync().thenAccept { success ->
    println("Web storage cleared: $success")
}

// Clear all browsing data at once
browser.storage.clearBrowsingDataAsync(
    clearCookies = true,
    clearStorage = true
)
```

## Java CompletableFuture Interop

All suspend cookie methods have `*Async` counterparts returning Java `CompletableFuture` for seamless Java interop.

```java
// Java: Read cookies asynchronously
engine.getCookieManager().getCookiesAsync("https://example.com")
    .thenAccept(cookies -> {
        System.out.println("Found " + cookies.size() + " cookies");
    });

// Java: Get all cookies across all domains
engine.getCookieManager().getAllCookiesAsync()
    .thenAccept(allCookies -> {
        for (KromiumCookie cookie : allCookies) {
            System.out.println(cookie.getName() + " = " + cookie.getValue());
        }
    });
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumCookieManager](/llms/api/kromium-cookie-manager.md)
- [KromiumCookie](/llms/api/kromium-cookie.md)
- [KromiumStorage](/llms/api/kromium-storage.md)

# Custom Protocol Scheme Handlers

> Register custom protocols (app://, kromium://) to serve web assets from the classpath, local directories, or dynamic handlers.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 8 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## How Custom Schemes Work

Custom schemes allow you to intercept `app://myapp/index.html` style URLs and serve content from JVM resources, local files, or dynamically generated responses. This enables building fully offline desktop apps with web UIs.

**Two-step process:**
1. **Register the scheme** with `KromiumCustomScheme` in `KromiumConfig` (before engine init).
2. **Register the handler** via `engine.registerSchemeHandler(...)` (after engine init).

## Registering a Custom Scheme

Custom schemes must be declared before engine initialization. Use `KromiumCustomScheme.secure()` for a secure scheme with CORS and Fetch API enabled, or construct with full control over security flags.

```kotlin
val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .browserConfig { b ->
        b.customSchemes(listOf(
            KromiumCustomScheme.secure("app"),
            KromiumCustomScheme(
                schemeName = "local",
                isStandard = true,
                isLocal = true,
                isSecure = true,
                isCorsEnabled = true,
                isCspBypassing = false,
                isFetchEnabled = true
            )
        ))
    }
    .build()
```

## Serving Assets from the Classpath

`KromiumSchemeHandler.fromClasspath()` creates a turnkey handler that streams resources bundled inside your application JAR. Supports SPA fallback routing for React/Vue/Angular apps.

```kotlin
val engine = Kromium.createEngine(config)
engine.initialize()

// Serve from src/main/resources/web/
val handler = KromiumSchemeHandler.fromClasspath(
    resourcePath = "web",
    spaFallback = "index.html"
)
engine.registerSchemeHandler("app", "myapp", handler)

// Now navigate to app://myapp/index.html
val browser = engine.createClient().createBrowser("app://myapp/index.html")
```

## Serving Assets from a Local Directory

`KromiumSchemeHandler.fromDirectory()` serves files from a local filesystem directory with built-in directory traversal protection and SPA fallback support.

```kotlin
val handler = KromiumSchemeHandler.fromDirectory(
    directory = File("./frontend/dist"),
    spaFallback = "index.html",
    defaultHeaders = mapOf(
        "X-Frame-Options" to "DENY"
    )
)
engine.registerSchemeHandler("app", "myapp", handler)
```

## Dynamic Custom Handlers

For dynamic content, implement `KromiumAssetHandler` directly. Return `KromiumAssetResponse.json()`, `.html()`, `.text()`, or `.stream()` — or `null` for 404.

```kotlin
val apiHandler = KromiumSchemeHandler.create { request ->
    when {
        request.path == "/api/user" -> {
            KromiumAssetResponse.json("""
                {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}
            """.trimIndent())
        }
        request.path.startsWith("/api/") -> {
            KromiumAssetResponse.notFound("Endpoint not found: ${request.path}")
        }
        else -> null // 404
    }
}
engine.registerSchemeHandler("app", "api", apiHandler)
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumCustomScheme](/llms/api/kromium-custom-scheme.md)
- [KromiumSchemeHandler](/llms/api/kromium-scheme-handler.md)
- [KromiumAssetHandler](/llms/api/kromium-asset-handler.md)
- [KromiumAssetRequest](/llms/api/kromium-asset-request.md)
- [KromiumAssetResponse](/llms/api/kromium-asset-response.md)

# PDF Export & Print API

> Export web pages to vector PDF documents with configurable paper size, margins, headers/footers, accessible tagging, and page ranges.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 5 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Basic PDF Export

Export any loaded web page to a PDF file using `browser.automation` with `KromiumPdfSettings`. The PDF is generated using Chromium's built-in print-to-PDF pipeline, producing high-quality vector output.

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.print.KromiumPdfSettings
import org.daviante.kromium.api.print.KromiumPaperSize
import java.io.File

// Wait for page to fully load first
browser.navigation.loadUrl("https://example.com", waitUntil = NavigationStage.LOADED)

// Export with default A4 portrait settings
val settings = KromiumPdfSettings.Default
browser.automation.printToPdf(File("output.pdf"), settings)
```

## Advanced PDF Configuration

Use the fluent `KromiumPdfSettings.builder()` for full control over orientation, background printing, custom paper sizes, margins, page ranges, and accessibility features.

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `landscape` | `Boolean` | `false` | Landscape orientation |
| `printBackground` | `Boolean` | `false` | Include CSS backgrounds and gradients |
| `scale` | `Double` | `1.0` | Page scaling (1.0 = 100%) |
| `paperSize` | `KromiumPaperSize` | `A4` | Paper dimensions |
| `margins` | `KromiumPdfMargins` | `Default` | Page margins |
| `pageRanges` | `String` | `""` | Pages to print (e.g. "1-5, 8") |
| `displayHeaderFooter` | `Boolean` | `false` | Show header/footer templates |
| `generateTaggedPdf` | `Boolean` | `false` | Accessible tagged PDF |
| `generateDocumentOutline` | `Boolean` | `false` | Bookmarks from headings |

```kotlin
val settings = KromiumPdfSettings.builder()
    .landscape(true)
    .printBackground(true)
    .paperSize(KromiumPaperSize.LETTER)
    .margins(KromiumPdfMargins(top = 1.0, bottom = 1.0, left = 0.5, right = 0.5))
    .pageRanges("1-3, 5")
    .displayHeaderFooter(true)
    .headerTemplate("<div style='font-size:8px;text-align:center;'>Company Report</div>")
    .footerTemplate("<div style='font-size:8px;text-align:center;'>Page <span class='pageNumber'></span> of <span class='totalPages'></span></div>")
    .generateTaggedPdf(true)
    .generateDocumentOutline(true)
    .createDirectories(true)
    .build()

browser.automation.printToPdf(File("reports/quarterly.pdf"), settings)
```

## Standard Paper Sizes

`KromiumPaperSize` provides constants for standard paper dimensions:
- `KromiumPaperSize.A4` — 210 × 297 mm (ISO standard)
- `KromiumPaperSize.LETTER` — 8.5 × 11 inches (US standard)
- `KromiumPaperSize.LEGAL` — 8.5 × 14 inches
- `KromiumPaperSize.TABLOID` — 11 × 17 inches
- Custom sizes via `KromiumPaperSize(widthInches, heightInches)`

## Related APIs

- [KromiumPdfSettings](/llms/api/kromium-pdf-settings.md)
- [KromiumPaperSize](/llms/api/kromium-paper-size.md)
- [KromiumPdfMargins](/llms/api/kromium-pdf-margins.md)
- [KromiumAutomation](/llms/api/kromium-automation.md)

# Context Menu Customization

> Suppress, customize, or build rich right-click context menus using KromiumMenuBuilder's declarative DSL with built-in browser action shortcuts.

- **Category:** UI
- **Read Time:** 6 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Built-In Preset Menus

`KromiumContextMenuListener` provides turnkey presets for common scenarios:

| Preset | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `KromiumContextMenuListener.disabled()` | Suppresses all context menus (kiosk mode) |
| `KromiumContextMenuListener.defaultMenu()` | Preserves native Chromium menu items |
| `KromiumContextMenuListener.devToolsOnly()` | Shows only "Inspect Element" |
| `KromiumContextMenuListener.minimalEditing()` | Smart menu: Copy Link on links, Copy/Search on selections, Cut/Paste/Select All in editable fields |

```kotlin
// Suppress all right-click menus
client.contextMenuListener = KromiumContextMenuListener.disabled()

// Or use the smart minimal editing menu with Inspect Element
client.contextMenuListener = KromiumContextMenuListener.minimalEditing(
    includeInspectElement = true
)
```

## Declarative Menu Builder DSL

Use `client.setContextMenu { ... }` with the `KromiumMenuBuilder` DSL to construct custom menus with items, checkboxes, radio buttons, submenus, and separators.

```kotlin
client.setContextMenu { ctx ->
    clear() // Remove default items

    item("Navigate Home") { it.browser.navigation.loadUrl("https://myapp.com") }
    separator()

    if (ctx.params.hasSelection()) {
        copy()
        searchWeb()
        separator()
    }

    if (ctx.params.isLink()) {
        copyLink()
        separator()
    }

    if (ctx.params.hasMedia()) {
        saveImageAs()
        copyImageUrl()
        separator()
    }

    subMenu("Developer") {
        inspectElement()
        viewSource()
        reload()
    }
}
```

## Built-In Action Shortcuts

KromiumMenuBuilder provides turnkey browser action methods that automatically wire up native commands:

| Method | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `back()` / `forward()` / `reload()` | Navigation commands |
| `copy()` / `cut()` / `paste()` / `selectAll()` | Clipboard commands |
| `print()` | Native print dialog |
| `viewSource()` | View page source |
| `inspectElement()` | Opens DevTools at click position |
| `copyLink()` | Copies the hovered link URL |
| `saveImageAs()` | Downloads the hovered image |
| `copyImageUrl()` | Copies the hovered image URL |
| `searchWeb()` | Searches Google for selected text |

## Java Usage

Context menu customization works identically in Java using `KromiumContextMenuListener` and the Consumer overloads of `addItem()`.

```java
client.setContextMenuListener(KromiumContextMenuListener.minimalEditing(true));

// Or custom:
client.setContextMenuListener((builder, context) -> {
    builder.clear();
    builder.addItem("Open Dashboard", ctx -> {
        ctx.getBrowser().getNavigation().loadUrl("https://dashboard.app");
    });
    builder.inspectElement();
});
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumContextMenuListener](/llms/api/kromium-context-menu-listener.md)
- [KromiumMenuBuilder](/llms/api/kromium-menu-builder.md)
- [KromiumContextMenuContext](/llms/api/kromium-context-menu-context.md)
- [KromiumContextMenuParams](/llms/api/kromium-context-menu-params.md)

# Error Handling & Debugging

> Handle Kromium's sealed exception hierarchy, recover from download failures, diagnose GPU errors, and monitor console messages for debugging.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 7 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## KromiumException Sealed Hierarchy

All Kromium errors extend the sealed class `KromiumException` which provides an `errorCode` (enum) and `isRecoverable` flag for programmatic error handling.

| Exception | Error Code | Recoverable | When Thrown |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `NotInitialized` | `INITIALIZATION_ERROR` | ❌ | Engine used before `initialize()` |
| `Disposed` | `INITIALIZATION_ERROR` | ❌ | Operations attempted after `dispose()` |
| `UnsupportedPlatform` | `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` | ❌ | Unsupported OS/architecture combination |
| `InstallationFailed` | `INSTALLATION_FAILED` | ✅ | Cannot prepare installation directory |
| `AutoDownloadDisabled` | `DOWNLOAD_DISABLED` | ❌ | No binaries and auto-download is off |
| `NoBundleAvailable` | `NO_BUNDLE_AVAILABLE` | ❌ | No compatible JCEF bundle for platform |
| `DownloadFailed` | `DOWNLOAD_FAILED` | ✅ | Network failure downloading engine |
| `ChecksumMismatch` | `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` | ✅ | Archive hash doesn't match (retry) |
| `ExtractionFailed` | `EXTRACTION_FAILED` | ✅ | Cannot extract engine archive |
| `MaliciousArchiveEntry` | `MALICIOUS_ARCHIVE` | ❌ | Directory traversal in archive |
| `BootstrapFailed` | `BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` | ❌ | CEF native bootstrap failure |
| `InstallationCorrupted` | `INSTALLATION_CORRUPTED` | ✅ | Corrupted binaries (re-download) |
| `JsEvaluationTimeout` | `JS_TIMEOUT` | ✅ | JavaScript evaluation timed out |
| `InvalidConfig` | `INVALID_CONFIG` | ❌ | Invalid configuration parameters |
| `ProxyError` | `PROXY_ERROR` | ✅ | Proxy configuration error |
| `PdfPrintFailed` | `PDF_PRINT_FAILED` | ✅ | PDF export failure |
| `FrameworkRequired` | `FRAMEWORK_REQUIRED` | ❌ | No UI framework specified for OSR |
| `CanvasNotAvailable` | `CANVAS_NOT_AVAILABLE` | ❌ | Missing kromium-swing/compose/etc on classpath |

## Pattern-Matching Error Recovery

Use Kotlin `when` exhaustive matching or Java `instanceof` checks on the sealed hierarchy for type-safe error recovery.

```kotlin
try {
    engine.initialize()
} catch (e: KromiumException) {
    when (e) {
        is KromiumException.DownloadFailed -> {
            println("Download failed from ${e.url}, retrying...")
            engine.initialize() // Retry
        }
        is KromiumException.ChecksumMismatch -> {
            println("Checksum mismatch: expected=${e.expected}, actual=${e.actual}")
            // Delete corrupted file and retry
        }
        is KromiumException.UnsupportedPlatform -> {
            println("Platform not supported: ${e.os} / ${e.arch}")
        }
        is KromiumException.CanvasNotAvailable -> {
            println("Add kromium-${e.framework.name.lowercase()} to your dependencies")
        }
        else -> {
            if (e.isRecoverable) {
                println("Recoverable error [${e.errorCode}]: ${e.message}")
            } else {
                throw e
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Console Message Monitoring

Intercept browser console output (`console.log`, `console.error`, `console.warn`) via `KromiumConsoleMessageListener` for runtime debugging and error tracking.

```kotlin
client.consoleMessageListener = KromiumConsoleMessageListener { message ->
    val level = message.level // INFO, WARNING, ERROR
    val text = message.message
    val source = message.source
    val line = message.lineNumber
    println("[$level] $source:$line — $text")
}
```

## Page Load Error Handling

Detect navigation failures (DNS errors, timeouts, certificate rejections) with `KromiumLoadErrorListener`.

```kotlin
client.loadErrorListener = KromiumLoadErrorListener { error ->
    println("Load error: ${error.errorCode} — ${error.errorText}")
    println("Failed URL: ${error.failedUrl}")
}
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumException](/llms/api/kromium-exception.md)
- [KromiumErrorCode](/llms/api/kromium-error-code.md)
- [KromiumConsoleMessage](/llms/api/kromium-console-message.md)
- [KromiumConsoleMessageListener](/llms/api/kromium-console-message-listener.md)
- [KromiumLoadError](/llms/api/kromium-load-error.md)
- [KromiumLoadErrorListener](/llms/api/kromium-load-error-listener.md)

# DevTools, Text Search & JavaScript Bridge

> Open Chromium DevTools, find text on pages, execute JavaScript, extract HTML/text content, and resolve favicons.

- **Category:** Core API
- **Read Time:** 5 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Opening Developer Tools

The `browser.devTools` facade provides direct control over the native Chromium Developer Tools window.

```kotlin
// Open DevTools (docked or undocked based on Chromium default)
browser.devTools.openDevTools()

// Open DevTools targeting a specific element at coordinates
browser.devTools.openDevTools(inspectPoint = Point(300, 200))

// Close DevTools
browser.devTools.closeDevTools()
```

## Find Text on Page

The `browser.search` facade provides in-page text search with highlighting, case sensitivity, and directional navigation — similar to Ctrl+F in a browser.

```kotlin
// Start a case-insensitive forward search
browser.search.find(
    searchText = "Kromium",
    forward = true,
    matchCase = false,
    findNext = false
)

// Navigate to the next match
browser.search.find(
    searchText = "Kromium",
    forward = true,
    findNext = true
)

// Navigate to the previous match
browser.search.find(
    searchText = "Kromium",
    forward = false,
    findNext = true
)

// Stop searching and clear highlights
browser.search.stopFinding(clearSelection = true)
```

## JavaScript Execution & Bridge

The `browser.jsBridge` facade provides bidirectional JavaScript interoperability with both fire-and-forget execution and async evaluated results.

```kotlin
// Fire-and-forget JavaScript execution
browser.jsBridge.executeJavaScript("document.title = 'Hello from Kotlin'")

// Evaluate and await a result (suspend)
val width = browser.jsBridge.evaluateJavaScript(
    "window.innerWidth * window.devicePixelRatio"
)
println("Viewport width: $width")

// Get full page HTML
val html = browser.jsBridge.getHtml()

// Get visible text content
val text = browser.jsBridge.getText()

// Resolve the page's favicon URL
val favicon = browser.jsBridge.getFaviconUrl()
```

## Java CompletableFuture Interop

All suspend JS bridge methods have `*Async` counterparts for Java interop.

```java
// Java: Get HTML asynchronously
browser.getJsBridge().getHtmlAsync()
    .thenAccept(html -> System.out.println("Page HTML length: " + html.length()));

// Java: Get text content
browser.getJsBridge().getTextAsync()
    .thenAccept(text -> System.out.println("Visible text: " + text));

// Java: Resolve favicon
browser.getJsBridge().getFaviconUrlAsync()
    .thenAccept(url -> System.out.println("Favicon: " + url));
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumDevTools](/llms/api/kromium-dev-tools.md)
- [KromiumSearch](/llms/api/kromium-search.md)
- [KromiumJsBridge](/llms/api/kromium-js-bridge.md)
- [KromiumConsoleMessage](/llms/api/kromium-console-message.md)

# Sample Applications & Reference Code

> Explore the 5 official Kromium desktop sample applications covering Compose Multiplatform, Swing, JavaFX, SWT, and AWT.

- **Category:** Getting Started
- **Read Time:** 8 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Official Sample Applications

The Kromium repository provides 5 fully functional desktop sample applications in the `samples/` directory. Each sample demonstrates production-grade architecture, theming, window management, and Kromium feature integration.

| Sample Application | Path | UI Framework | Features Covered |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`kromium-sample-compose`** | `samples/kromium-sample-compose` | Compose Multiplatform (Desktop) | 9 Feature Panels: Automation, Cookies/Storage, DevTools, DOM Extraction, Downloads, Navigation, PDF Print, Security/Network, View Tools |
| **`kromium-sample-swing`** | `samples/kromium-sample-swing` | Java Swing | 9 Feature Panels with custom dark/light theme, card components, traffic light window controls, and logging console |
| **`kromium-sample-javafx`** | `samples/kromium-sample-javafx` | OpenJFX / JavaFX | FXML-free declarative Kotlin UI, TabPane navigation, hardware texture blitting, and automation |
| **`kromium-sample-swt`** | `samples/kromium-sample-swt` | Eclipse SWT | SWT Composite embedding, native OS event loop integration, key event bridge, and developer tools |
| **`kromium-sample-awt`** | `samples/kromium-sample-awt` | Pure Java AWT | Minimalist dependency-free browser, Java2D BufferedImage blitting, and navigation controls |

## Running the Samples

You can launch any sample directly from the root repository using Gradle:

```bash
# Run Compose Multiplatform sample
./gradlew :samples:kromium-sample-compose:run

# Run Swing sample
./gradlew :samples:kromium-sample-swing:run

# Run JavaFX sample
./gradlew :samples:kromium-sample-javafx:run

# Run Eclipse SWT sample
./gradlew :samples:kromium-sample-swt:run

# Run Pure AWT sample
./gradlew :samples:kromium-sample-awt:run
```

## Compose Multiplatform Sample Architecture

Located at `samples/kromium-sample-compose`, this sample demonstrates how to build a tabbed developer workbench using Compose Desktop with reactive StateFlow collection.

```kotlin
// From samples/kromium-sample-compose/src/main/kotlin/org/daviante/kromium/sample/Main.kt
fun main() = application {
    val engine = remember { Kromium.createEngine() }
    DisposableEffect(Unit) {
        engine.initialize()
        onDispose { engine.dispose() }
    }

    val client = remember(engine) { engine.createClient() }
    val browser = remember(client) {
        client.createBrowser(
            url = "https://example.com",
            framework = KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE
        )
    }

    Window(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "Kromium Compose Sample") {
        SampleAppShell(browser = browser)
    }
}
```

## Swing Sample Architecture & UI Shell

Located at `samples/kromium-sample-swing`, this sample illustrates embedding `KromiumSwingCanvas` inside a custom-themed Swing layout with `BorderLayout` and custom swing components.

```kotlin
// From samples/kromium-sample-swing/src/main/kotlin/org/daviante/kromium/sample/swing/Main.kt
SwingUtilities.invokeLater {
    val engine = Kromium.createEngine()
    engine.initialize()

    val client = engine.createClient()
    val browser = client.createBrowser(
        url = "https://example.com",
        framework = KromiumUiFramework.SWING
    )

    val frame = JFrame("Kromium Swing Sample")
    frame.defaultCloseOperation = JFrame.EXIT_ON_CLOSE
    frame.setSize(1400, 900)

    val canvas = browser.view.surface.unwrap(Component::class.java) as JPanel
    frame.contentPane.add(canvas, BorderLayout.CENTER)
    frame.isVisible = true
}
```

## Feature Code Samples in the Repository

The sample applications contain dedicated feature files that developers can directly copy into their projects:

- **`AutomationFeature.kt`**: Automatic form filling, clicking buttons by CSS selector, typing into inputs, and dispatching keyboard events.
- **`CookieStorageFeature.kt`**: Reading/setting cookies, inspecting Local Storage, and clearing browser cache.
- **`DevToolsFeature.kt`**: Launching undocked DevTools window, inspecting specific elements, and measuring page performance.
- **`DomExtractionFeature.kt`**: Extracting page title, outer HTML, text content, and resolving dynamic elements.
- **`DownloadsFeature.kt`**: Intercepting download items, tracking download speed and bytes received, and pausing/canceling.
- **`NavigationFeature.kt`**: URL loading, back/forward history, stop/reload, and navigation stage state listeners.
- **`PdfPrintFeature.kt`**: Vector PDF generation with custom margins, paper sizes, and headers/footers.
- **`SecurityNetworkFeature.kt`**: Custom SOCKS5/HTTP proxy setup, SSL certificate exception handling, and media permissions.
- **`ViewToolsFeature.kt`**: Zoom level manipulation, window resizing, and screenshot capture.

- [KromiumUiFramework](/llms/api/kromium-ui-framework.md)
- [KromiumView](/llms/api/kromium-view.md)
- [KromiumBrowser](/llms/api/kromium-browser.md)

# Troubleshooting & FAQ

> Solutions for JVM module access errors, GPU rasterization failures, VM/Docker environments, and platform-specific native dependencies.

- **Category:** Getting Started
- **Read Time:** 7 min
- **Last Updated:** 2026-10-01

## Java 9+ JVM Module Access (--add-opens)

On Java 9 and newer, Java Strong Encapsulation restricts reflection into internal `sun.awt` and `sun.java2d` packages. Kromium includes `KromiumJvmModuleOpener` which attempts to open these modules dynamically at runtime. However, if your application runs under strict modularity or custom security managers, add the following JVM flags to your Gradle build or startup scripts:

```bash
--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.awt=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.java2d=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.awt.windows=ALL-UNNAMED # Windows only
--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.lwawt=ALL-UNNAMED      # macOS only
--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.awt.X11=ALL-UNNAMED    # Linux only
```

In Gradle `build.gradle.kts`:
```kotlin
application {
    applicationDefaultJvmArgs = listOf(
        "--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.awt=ALL-UNNAMED",
        "--add-opens=java.desktop/sun.java2d=ALL-UNNAMED"
    )
}
```

## GPU Device Loss, VM & CI Rendering Failures

If you encounter Direct3D device reset errors (`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`, `0x887a0005`) on Windows or are running in virtual machines, Docker containers, or headless CI runners without physical GPUs, configure `KromiumGpuMode.SOFTWARE` or `KromiumGpuMode.ANGLE_WARP` in `KromiumHardwareConfig`.

```kotlin
val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .hardwareConfig { hw ->
        // On Windows with overclocked/unstable drivers:
        // hw.gpuMode(KromiumGpuMode.ANGLE_WARP)

        // In headless CI or VMs without GPU drivers:
        hw.gpuMode(KromiumGpuMode.SOFTWARE)
    }
    .build()
```

## Linux Native Library Requirements

Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) requires native shared libraries on Linux. If the engine fails to initialize on Debian/Ubuntu, install the required packages:

```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y \
    libnss3 \
    libatk1.0-0 \
    libatk-bridge2.0-0 \
    libcups2 \
    libxcomposite1 \
    libxdamage1 \
    libxfixes3 \
    libxrandr2 \
    libgbm1 \
    libasound2 \
    libpango-1.0-0 \
    libpangocairo-1.0-0
```

## Process Model & Compose Desktop Compatibility

Always keep `KromiumProcessModel.AUTO` (the default) when embedding in Jetpack Compose, Swing, or JavaFX. In `AUTO` mode, Kromium executes the browser host inside the JVM while spawning `jcef_helper` subprocesses for GPU rasterization and web page sandboxing. Avoid `OUT_OF_PROCESS` unless you implement a custom `CefNativeRenderHandler`.

## Capturing Chromium Diagnostic Logs

To diagnose native crashes, network handshakes, or certificate errors, enable verbose logging and specify a dedicated log file path.

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumLogSeverity
import java.io.File

val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .loggingConfig { log ->
        log.severity(KromiumLogSeverity.VERBOSE)
        log.logFile(File("./logs/chromium-debug.log"))
    }
    .build()
```

## Related APIs

- [KromiumGpuMode](/llms/api/kromium-gpu-mode.md)
- [KromiumProcessModel](/llms/api/kromium-process-model.md)
- [KromiumLoggingConfig](/llms/api/kromium-logging-config.md)
- [KromiumException](/llms/api/kromium-exception.md)

# Kromium

```kotlin
object Kromium
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api`
- **Category:** Core Engine
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

The main entry point for the Kromium library. Provides synchronized factory access to create and manage the active singleton KromiumEngine instance using a specified KromiumConfig and KromiumEngineProvider.

### When to Use

Call Kromium.createEngine(config, provider) during application bootstrap to create the shared uninitialized KromiumEngine instance.

## Methods

### `createEngine()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic @Synchronized fun createEngine(config: KromiumConfig, provider: KromiumEngineProvider): KromiumEngine
```

Creates the Kromium engine using the provided configuration and provider. The engine is NOT automatically initialized. You must call engine.initialize() on a background thread so you can observe engine.state from the UI.

- **Returns:** `KromiumEngine`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.Kromium
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.jcef.JcefProvider

val config = KromiumConfig.builder().build()
val engine = Kromium.createEngine(config, JcefProvider)
engine.initialize()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.Kromium;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine;
import org.daviante.kromium.jcef.JcefProvider;

KromiumConfig config = KromiumConfig.builder().build();
KromiumEngine engine = Kromium.createEngine(config, JcefProvider.INSTANCE);
engine.initializeAsync();
```


---

# KromiumEngine

```kotlin
interface KromiumEngine
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.core`
- **Category:** Core Engine
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

The core interface representing the running Kromium engine. Manages lifecycle states, native binary initialization and disposal, browser client sessions, global cookie management, scheme handler registration, and engine-wide download operations.

### When to Use

Obtain via Kromium.createEngine(config, provider) or provider.createEngine(config) to control the engine lifecycle, observe states via StateFlow, and spawn isolated KromiumClient sessions.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`state`** | `StateFlow<KromiumState>` | The current state of the engine (e.g. downloading, extracting, ready). |
| **`info`** | `KromiumEngineInfo` | Gets information about the current engine installation. |
| **`cookieManager`** | `KromiumCookieManager` | Global cookie manager for this engine. |

## Methods

### `initialize()`

```kotlin
suspend fun initialize()
```

Initializes the engine asynchronously, downloading/extracting binaries if necessary.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

### `initializeAsync()`

```kotlin
fun initializeAsync(): CompletableFuture<Void?>
```

Asynchronously initializes the engine returning a Java CompletableFuture.

- **Returns:** `CompletableFuture<Void?>`

### `dispose()`

```kotlin
fun dispose()
```

Disposes the engine, cleaning up native resources.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

### `createClient()`

```kotlin
fun createClient(config: KromiumClientConfig = KromiumClientConfig.default()): KromiumClient
```

Creates a new isolated browser client session.

- **Returns:** `KromiumClient`

### `registerSchemeHandler()`

```kotlin
fun registerSchemeHandler(schemeName: String, domainName: String? = null, handler: KromiumAssetHandler): Boolean
```

Registers a custom protocol scheme handler factory with the engine.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `cancelDownload()`

```kotlin
fun cancelDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Programmatically cancels an in-progress download identified by its download ID across any active browser session.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `pauseDownload()`

```kotlin
fun pauseDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Programmatically pauses an in-progress download identified by its download ID across any active browser session.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `resumeDownload()`

```kotlin
fun resumeDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Programmatically resumes a paused download identified by its download ID across any active browser session.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `isDownloadPaused()`

```kotlin
fun isDownloadPaused(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Checks whether an in-progress download is currently paused across any active browser session.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `clearSchemeHandlers()`

```kotlin
fun clearSchemeHandlers(): Boolean
```

Clears all registered custom scheme handler factories.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.jcef.JcefProvider

suspend fun initEngine() {
    val engine = JcefProvider.createEngine(KromiumConfig.builder().build())
    engine.initialize()
    val client = engine.createClient()
}
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine;
import org.daviante.kromium.jcef.JcefProvider;

public class EngineInit {
    public static void start() {
        KromiumEngine engine = JcefProvider.INSTANCE.createEngine(KromiumConfig.builder().build());
        engine.initializeAsync().thenRun(() -> {
            System.out.println("Engine ready!");
        });
    }
}
```

# KromiumBrowser

```kotlin
interface KromiumBrowser : AutoCloseable
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.core`
- **Category:** Browser & Client Components
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Main interface for the Kromium browser instance. Structured into multiple dedicated facades for separation of concerns: navigation, view, search, devTools, jsBridge, clipboard, downloads, automation, storage, proxyManager, security, and assets.

### When to Use

Obtain via client.createBrowser() to render, control, and interact with a Chromium web view instance.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`navigation`** | `KromiumNavigation` | Facade for URL loading, lifecycle waiting (DOMContentLoaded, NetworkIdle), and history traversal. |
| **`view`** | `KromiumView` | Facade for zoom control, audio muting, viewport resizing, and rendering visibility. |
| **`search`** | `KromiumSearch` | Facade for finding text on page, highlighting matches, and navigating find results. |
| **`devTools`** | `KromiumDevTools` | Facade for opening and closing the native Chromium Developer Tools window. |
| **`jsBridge`** | `KromiumJsBridge` | Facade for bidirectional JavaScript interoperability, script execution, and native object binding. |
| **`clipboard`** | `KromiumClipboard` | Facade for clipboard operations (cut, copy, paste, select all, undo, redo). |
| **`downloads`** | `KromiumDownloads` | Facade for managing and controlling file downloads. |
| **`automation`** | `KromiumAutomation` | Facade for headless automation, mouse/keyboard simulation, DOM querying, and PDF export. |
| **`storage`** | `KromiumStorage` | Facade for cache management, local storage inspection, and cookie clearing. |
| **`proxyManager`** | `KromiumProxyManager` | Facade for runtime dynamic proxy reconfiguration. |
| **`security`** | `KromiumSecurity` | Facade for host locking, subresource restrictions, and iframe security. |
| **`assets`** | `KromiumAssets` | Facade for dynamic network asset filtering and content blocking. |

## Methods

### `close()`

```kotlin
override fun close()
```

Closes this browser instance and cleans up underlying resources.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumBrowser
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumClient
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework

fun setupBrowser(client: KromiumClient): KromiumBrowser {
    val browser = client.createBrowser("https://github.com", KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE)
    browser.navigation.loadUrl("https://google.com")
    return browser
}
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumBrowser;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumClient;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework;

public class BrowserCreator {
    public static void create(KromiumClient client) {
        try (KromiumBrowser browser = client.createBrowser("https://example.com", KromiumUiFramework.SWING)) {
            browser.getNavigation().loadUrl("https://example.com");
        }
    }
}
```


---

# KromiumClient

```kotlin
interface KromiumClient
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.core`
- **Category:** Browser & Client Components
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Represents a client session in the engine. A client groups multiple browsers under a shared context (such as shared cookies, cache, proxy configuration, network request interceptors, and listeners).

### When to Use

Obtain via engine.createClient(config) to group browser instances with custom session interceptors, listeners, proxy rules, and download configurations.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`inFlightRequestCount`** | `Int` | The number of active, in-flight network requests across all browsers in this client. |
| **`downloadListener`** | `KromiumDownloadListener?` | Listener for tracking global download progress. |
| **`downloadDirectory`** | `File` | The default directory where downloads should be saved. |
| **`onBeforeDownloadListener`** | `KromiumBeforeDownloadListener?` | Optional interceptor to dynamically resolve the target path before a download begins. Return null to use default path, or return empty string "" to cancel. |
| **`doNotTrack`** | `Boolean` | Whether to assert Do Not Track (DNT) and Global Privacy Control (Sec-GPC) headers on outbound requests. |
| **`rememberPermissions`** | `Boolean` | Whether permission decisions (e.g. camera, microphone) should be cached for the lifetime of this client session. |
| **`requestInterceptor`** | `KromiumRequestInterceptor?` | Request interceptor for filtering or modifying outgoing HTTP/HTTPS requests. |
| **`navigationInterceptor`** | `KromiumNavigationInterceptor?` | Interceptor for evaluating and potentially overriding top-level navigation. |
| **`authListener`** | `KromiumAuthListener?` | Listener for HTTP authentication challenges. |
| **`popupListener`** | `KromiumPopupListener?` | Listener for popup window requests. |
| **`jsDialogListener`** | `KromiumJsDialogListener?` | Listener for JavaScript dialogs (alert, confirm, prompt). |
| **`enableContextMenus`** | `Boolean` | Globally enables or disables native right-click context menus for this client. Defaults to true. |
| **`contextMenuListener`** | `KromiumContextMenuListener?` | Listener for context menu events and custom menu construction. |
| **`permissionListener`** | `KromiumPermissionListener?` | Listener for media/device permission requests. |
| **`consoleMessageListener`** | `KromiumConsoleMessageListener?` | Listener for browser console messages. |
| **`loadErrorListener`** | `KromiumLoadErrorListener?` | Listener for page load errors. |
| **`currentProxy`** | `KromiumProxy?` | The currently active proxy configuration for this client session, or null if no custom proxy has been set. |

## Methods

### `createBrowser()`

```kotlin
fun createBrowser(url: String, config: KromiumClientConfig = KromiumClientConfig.default()): KromiumBrowser
```

Creates a new browser instance managed by this client.

- **Returns:** `KromiumBrowser`

### `createBrowser()`

```kotlin
fun createBrowser(url: String, framework: KromiumUiFramework): KromiumBrowser
```

Creates a new browser instance managed by this client with an explicit UI framework.

- **Returns:** `KromiumBrowser`

### `hasPendingRequests()`

```kotlin
fun hasPendingRequests(): Boolean
```

Whether there are any pending network requests active on this client.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `timeSinceLastRequestMs()`

```kotlin
fun timeSinceLastRequestMs(): Long
```

The number of milliseconds elapsed since the last network request completed.

- **Returns:** `Long`

### `setContextMenu()`

```kotlin
fun setContextMenu(block: KromiumMenuBuilder.(KromiumContextMenuContext) -> Unit)
```

Configures the right-click context menu using a declarative builder block.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

### `updateProxy()`

```kotlin
fun updateProxy(proxy: KromiumProxy): Boolean
```

Dynamically updates the proxy settings for this client session.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `clearPermissionCache()`

```kotlin
fun clearPermissionCache()
```

Clears all remembered permission decisions from the in-memory session cache.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

### `cancelDownload()`

```kotlin
fun cancelDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Cancels an active download by its ID.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `pauseDownload()`

```kotlin
fun pauseDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Pauses an active download by its ID.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `resumeDownload()`

```kotlin
fun resumeDownload(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Resumes a paused download by its ID.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `isDownloadPaused()`

```kotlin
fun isDownloadPaused(downloadId: Int): Boolean
```

Checks if a download is currently paused.

- **Returns:** `Boolean`

### `dispose()`

```kotlin
fun dispose()
```

Disposes the client and all associated browsers.

- **Returns:** `Unit`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumClient
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumBrowser
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework

fun createClientSession(engine: KromiumEngine): KromiumBrowser {
    val client: KromiumClient = engine.createClient()
    client.enableContextMenus = true
    return client.createBrowser("https://github.com", KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE)
}
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumClient;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumBrowser;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework;

public class ClientSetup {
    public static KromiumBrowser setup(KromiumEngine engine) {
        KromiumClient client = engine.createClient();
        return client.createBrowser("https://example.com", KromiumUiFramework.SWING);
    }
}
```

# KromiumState

```kotlin
sealed class KromiumState
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.core`
- **Category:** Core Engine
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Observable lifecycle and operational states of the Kromium engine emitted by KromiumEngine.state StateFlow.

### When to Use

Observe engine.state in UI layers (Compose Multiplatform, JavaFX, Swing) to display progress indicators, download status, or error messages before browser creation.

## States & Variants

| Variant | Declaration | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`KromiumState.Idle`** | `data object Idle : KromiumState()` | Engine has not started initialization or download. |
| **`KromiumState.Locating`** | `data object Locating : KromiumState()` | Locating local JCEF engine binaries on the system. |
| **`KromiumState.Downloading`** | `data class Downloading(val progress: KromiumDownloadProgress) : KromiumState()` | Downloading native JCEF bundle binaries with reactive progress metrics. |
| **`KromiumState.Extracting`** | `data object Extracting : KromiumState()` | Extracting downloaded bundle archive to the local cache directory. |
| **`KromiumState.Initializing`** | `data object Initializing : KromiumState()` | Bootstrapping CEF native binaries and preparing Chromium subsystems. |
| **`KromiumState.Ready`** | `data object Ready : KromiumState()` | CEF native runtime is initialized, healthy, and ready to create browser instances. |
| **`KromiumState.Error`** | `data class Error(val cause: Throwable) : KromiumState()` | Engine initialization or operational failure occurred; inspect cause for details. |
| **`KromiumState.Disposed`** | `data object Disposed : KromiumState()` | Engine and all associated browser instances have been disposed and shut down. |

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.*
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumState

@Composable
fun ObserveState(engine: KromiumEngine) {
    val state by engine.state.collectAsState()
    when (val s = state) {
        is KromiumState.Downloading -> println("Downloading: ${s.progress.fraction * 100}%")
        is KromiumState.Ready -> println("Engine ready")
        is KromiumState.Error -> println("Failed: ${s.cause.message}")
        else -> println("State: $s")
    }
}
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumEngine;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.core.KromiumState;

public class StateObserver {
    public static void check(KromiumEngine engine) {
        KromiumState state = engine.getState().getValue();
        if (state instanceof KromiumState.Ready) {
            System.out.println("Ready!");
        }
    }
}
```

# KromiumConfig

```kotlin
@ConsistentCopyVisibility data class KromiumConfig internal constructor(val downloadConfig: KromiumEngineDownloadConfig, val browserConfig: KromiumBrowserConfig, val hardwareConfig: KromiumHardwareConfig, val securityConfig: KromiumSecurityConfig, val loggingConfig: KromiumLoggingConfig)
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.config`
- **Category:** Configuration
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

The master configuration object for the Kromium engine. Composed of specialized domain sub-configurations for engine downloading, general browser parameters, hardware/GPU acceleration, enterprise security, and logging severity.

### When to Use

Instantiate via KromiumConfig.builder() to configure the engine prior to calling Kromium.createEngine(config, provider) or provider.createEngine(config).

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`downloadConfig`** | `KromiumEngineDownloadConfig` | Engine downloading, CDN release channels, and installation path configurations. |
| **`browserConfig`** | `KromiumBrowserConfig` | General browser settings, cache directory, remote debugging port, proxy, and custom schemes. |
| **`hardwareConfig`** | `KromiumHardwareConfig` | Host OS process model and GPU hardware acceleration options. |
| **`securityConfig`** | `KromiumSecurityConfig` | Chromium sandbox controls, telemetry blockers, WebRTC IP policies, and HTTP auth allowlists. |
| **`loggingConfig`** | `KromiumLoggingConfig` | Engine native logging severity level and log destination settings. |

## Methods

### `validate()`

```kotlin
fun validate()
```

Validates this configuration and throws KromiumException.InvalidConfig if any values are invalid (e.g. remoteDebuggingPort outside 0..65535 or path traversal in cachePath).

- **Returns:** `Unit`
- **Throws:** `KromiumException.InvalidConfig`

### `builder()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder
```

Returns a new builder for KromiumConfig initialized with default values.

- **Returns:** `Builder`

## Exceptions

| Exception | When Thrown |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`KromiumException.InvalidConfig`** |  |

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumGpuMode

val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .browserConfig { it.remoteDebuggingPort(9222) }
    .hardwareConfig { it.gpuMode(KromiumGpuMode.HARDWARE) }
    .securityConfig { it.sandboxEnabled(true).doNotTrack(true) }
    .build()

config.validate()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumConfig;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumBrowserConfig;

public class ConfigFactory {
    public static KromiumConfig create() {
        KromiumBrowserConfig browserConfig = KromiumBrowserConfig.builder()
            .remoteDebuggingPort(9222)
            .build();

        return KromiumConfig.builder()
            .browserConfig(browserConfig)
            .build();
    }
}
```

# KromiumBrowserConfig

```kotlin
@ConsistentCopyVisibility data class KromiumBrowserConfig internal constructor(val cachePath: String?, val isHeadless: Boolean, val remoteDebuggingPort: Int, val commandLineArgs: List<String>, val customSchemes: List<KromiumCustomScheme>, val schemeRegistrations: List<KromiumSchemeRegistration> = emptyList(), val proxy: KromiumProxy? = null)
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.config`
- **Category:** Configuration
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

General browser behavior and storage configuration for the Kromium engine. Controls disk cache directories, headless rendering mode, remote CDP debugging port, command-line arguments, custom URL scheme definitions, and default proxy rules.

### When to Use

Configure within KromiumConfig.builder().browserConfig { ... } to define engine-wide caching, debugging ports, and startup flags.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`cachePath`** | `String?` | Filesystem path where persistent cache and storage are kept, or null for in-memory incognito cache. |
| **`isHeadless`** | `Boolean` | Whether the engine operates in headless mode without desktop window handles. |
| **`remoteDebuggingPort`** | `Int` | Port for Chromium Remote Debugging Protocol (0 disables remote debugging). |
| **`commandLineArgs`** | `List<String>` | Additional native Chromium command-line switches passed during process initialization. |
| **`customSchemes`** | `List<KromiumCustomScheme>` | Custom URL schemes (e.g. app, res) registered with Chromium prior to engine startup. |
| **`schemeRegistrations`** | `List<KromiumSchemeRegistration>` | Initial custom scheme handler registrations binding asset handlers to scheme and domain names. |
| **`proxy`** | `KromiumProxy?` | Default proxy strategy applied to the engine and all client sessions. |

## Methods

### `builder()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder
```

Returns a new builder for KromiumBrowserConfig.

- **Returns:** `Builder`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumBrowserConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.api.proxy.KromiumProxy

val browserConfig = KromiumBrowserConfig.builder()
    .cachePath("/tmp/kromium-cache")
    .remoteDebuggingPort(9222)
    .proxy(KromiumProxy.system())
    .addArgs("--disable-gpu-shader-disk-cache", "--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required")
    .build()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumBrowserConfig;

public class BrowserConfigSetup {
    public static KromiumBrowserConfig create() {
        return KromiumBrowserConfig.builder()
            .isHeadless(false)
            .remoteDebuggingPort(9222)
            .build();
    }
}
```

# KromiumClientConfig

```kotlin
data class KromiumClientConfig(val userAgent: String? = null, val emulateDesktopEnvironment: Boolean = false, val doNotTrack: Boolean = true, val isIsolated: Boolean = false, val proxy: KromiumProxy? = null, val onBeforeDownloadListener: KromiumBeforeDownloadListener? = null, val downloadListener: KromiumDownloadListener? = null, val requestInterceptor: KromiumRequestInterceptor? = null, val navigationInterceptor: KromiumNavigationInterceptor? = null, val consoleMessageListener: KromiumConsoleMessageListener? = null, val jsDialogListener: KromiumJsDialogListener? = null, val popupListener: KromiumPopupListener? = null, val authListener: KromiumAuthListener? = null, val contextMenuListener: KromiumContextMenuListener? = null, val permissionListener: KromiumPermissionListener? = null, val loadErrorListener: KromiumLoadErrorListener? = null, val isOffScreenRendered: Boolean = true, val isTransparent: Boolean = false, val framework: KromiumUiFramework? = null, val sslErrorPolicy: SslErrorPolicy = SslErrorPolicy.Strict, val initialWidth: Int = 1280, val initialHeight: Int = 800)
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.config`
- **Category:** Configuration
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Configuration for a specific browser client session. Determines proxy settings, user agents, transparency, OSR canvas bindings, SSL error policies, initial dimensions, and event listeners for network, downloads, and UI interactions.

### When to Use

Pass into engine.createClient(config) or client.createBrowser(url, config) to configure individual browsing sessions.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`userAgent`** | `String?` | Custom HTTP User-Agent string, or null to use Chromium default. |
| **`emulateDesktopEnvironment`** | `Boolean` | Whether to emulate a standard desktop display environment. |
| **`doNotTrack`** | `Boolean` | Whether to send DNT: 1 and Sec-GPC: 1 privacy headers. |
| **`isIsolated`** | `Boolean` | Whether this client operates in an isolated incognito storage partition. |
| **`proxy`** | `KromiumProxy?` | Session-specific proxy configuration overriding the global engine proxy. |
| **`onBeforeDownloadListener`** | `KromiumBeforeDownloadListener?` | Callback to resolve target paths or cancel file downloads before transfer begins. |
| **`downloadListener`** | `KromiumDownloadListener?` | Callback to monitor file download progress and completion events. |
| **`requestInterceptor`** | `KromiumRequestInterceptor?` | Interceptor for inspecting, modifying, or blocking outgoing HTTP/HTTPS web resource requests. |
| **`navigationInterceptor`** | `KromiumNavigationInterceptor?` | Interceptor for evaluating and overriding top-level frame navigations. |
| **`consoleMessageListener`** | `KromiumConsoleMessageListener?` | Listener for JavaScript console messages (log, info, warn, error). |
| **`jsDialogListener`** | `KromiumJsDialogListener?` | Listener to handle or suppress JavaScript alert, confirm, and prompt dialogs. |
| **`popupListener`** | `KromiumPopupListener?` | Listener for popup window requests (window.open). |
| **`authListener`** | `KromiumAuthListener?` | Listener for HTTP Basic/Digest and proxy authentication challenges. |
| **`contextMenuListener`** | `KromiumContextMenuListener?` | Listener for right-click context menu construction and customization. |
| **`permissionListener`** | `KromiumPermissionListener?` | Listener for camera, microphone, screen share, and media device permission requests. |
| **`loadErrorListener`** | `KromiumLoadErrorListener?` | Listener for frame load failures, DNS resolution errors, and connection dropouts. |
| **`isOffScreenRendered`** | `Boolean` | Whether browsers in this client use off-screen rendering (OSR) into pixel buffers. |
| **`isTransparent`** | `Boolean` | Whether the web view canvas background is transparent. |
| **`framework`** | `KromiumUiFramework?` | Target UI framework (COMPOSE, SWING, JAVAFX, SWT, AWT) for OSR canvas factory resolution. |
| **`sslErrorPolicy`** | `SslErrorPolicy` | SSL certificate verification policy (Strict, IgnoreAll, AllowHostList, Custom). |
| **`initialWidth`** | `Int` | Initial viewport width in pixels. |
| **`initialHeight`** | `Int` | Initial viewport height in pixels. |

## Methods

### `default()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun default(): KromiumClientConfig
```

Returns the default client configuration instance.

- **Returns:** `KromiumClientConfig`

### `builder()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder
```

Returns a new builder for KromiumClientConfig.

- **Returns:** `Builder`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumClientConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework

val clientConfig = KromiumClientConfig.builder()
    .framework(KromiumUiFramework.COMPOSE)
    .doNotTrack(true)
    .initialWidth(1400)
    .initialHeight(900)
    .build()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumClientConfig;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.ui.KromiumUiFramework;

public class ClientConfigFactory {
    public static KromiumClientConfig create() {
        return KromiumClientConfig.builder()
            .framework(KromiumUiFramework.SWING)
            .doNotTrack(true)
            .build();
    }
}
```

# KromiumHardwareConfig

```kotlin
@ConsistentCopyVisibility data class KromiumHardwareConfig internal constructor(val processModel: KromiumProcessModel, val gpuMode: KromiumGpuMode)
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.config`
- **Category:** Configuration
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Controls how the engine interacts with the host OS and GPU. Configures Chromium process isolation architecture and graphics rendering acceleration mode.

### When to Use

Configure within KromiumConfig.builder().hardwareConfig { ... } to enable full GPU acceleration, disable GPU compositing, or activate software fallbacks in virtual machines.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`processModel`** | `KromiumProcessModel` | The process isolation architecture: AUTO (multi-process helper), OUT_OF_PROCESS (external RPC daemon), or IN_PROCESS (embedded). |
| **`gpuMode`** | `KromiumGpuMode` | Graphics rendering strategy: HARDWARE (full GPU), SOFTWARE (SwiftShader), COMPOSITING_DISABLED (CPU compositing), or ANGLE_WARP (Direct3D 11 WARP). |

## Methods

### `builder()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder
```

Returns a new builder for KromiumHardwareConfig.

- **Returns:** `Builder`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumHardwareConfig
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumProcessModel
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumGpuMode

val hardwareConfig = KromiumHardwareConfig.builder()
    .processModel(KromiumProcessModel.AUTO)
    .gpuMode(KromiumGpuMode.HARDWARE)
    .build()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumHardwareConfig;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumProcessModel;
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumGpuMode;

public class HardwareSetup {
    public static KromiumHardwareConfig create() {
        return KromiumHardwareConfig.builder()
            .processModel(KromiumProcessModel.AUTO)
            .gpuMode(KromiumGpuMode.HARDWARE)
            .build();
    }
}
```

# KromiumSecurityConfig

```kotlin
@ConsistentCopyVisibility data class KromiumSecurityConfig internal constructor(val sandboxEnabled: Boolean, val blockRegistryAndTelemetry: Boolean, val doNotTrack: Boolean, val webrtcIpHandlingPolicy: String?, val authServerAllowlist: List<String>, val authNegotiateDelegateAllowlist: List<String>)
```

- **Module:** `kromium-api`
- **Package:** `org.daviante.kromium.api.config`
- **Category:** Configuration
- **Since Version:** v1.0.0.150-b11

## Description

Handles security boundaries, privacy headers, WebRTC IP leak prevention, enterprise NTLM/Kerberos authentication allowlists, and background telemetry blocking.

### When to Use

Configure within KromiumConfig.builder().securityConfig { ... } to lock down browser security, protect user privacy, or configure corporate SSO authentication.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`sandboxEnabled`** | `Boolean` | Whether native Chromium sandboxing is enforced. |
| **`blockRegistryAndTelemetry`** | `Boolean` | Whether to block Windows registry touchpoints and outgoing background telemetry (metrics, crash reports). |
| **`doNotTrack`** | `Boolean` | Whether DNT: 1 and Sec-GPC: 1 privacy headers are asserted. |
| **`webrtcIpHandlingPolicy`** | `String?` | WebRTC IP handling policy to prevent local/private IP address leaks (e.g. disable_non_proxied_udp). |
| **`authServerAllowlist`** | `List<String>` | Allowlist of servers permitted for integrated HTTP Windows authentication (NTLM/Kerberos). |
| **`authNegotiateDelegateAllowlist`** | `List<String>` | Allowlist of servers to which Kerberos credentials can be delegated. |

## Methods

### `builder()`

```kotlin
@JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder
```

Returns a new builder for KromiumSecurityConfig.

- **Returns:** `Builder`

## Code Examples

### Compose Multiplatform (kotlin)

```kotlin
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumSecurityConfig

val securityConfig = KromiumSecurityConfig.builder()
    .sandboxEnabled(true)
    .blockRegistryAndTelemetry(true)
    .doNotTrack(true)
    .webrtcIpHandlingPolicy("disable_non_proxied_udp")
    .authServerAllowlist(listOf("*.corp.internal"))
    .build()
```

### Pure Java (java)

```java
import org.daviante.kromium.api.config.KromiumSecurityConfig;
import java.util.List;

public class SecuritySetup {
    public static KromiumSecurityConfig create() {
        return KromiumSecurityConfig.builder()
            .sandboxEnabled(true)
            .doNotTrack(true)
            .authServerAllowlist(List.of("*.corp.internal"))
            .build();
    }
}
```
